//: Every skip the browser suite is permitted to take, keyed by a stable capability id.
A skip is a statement that a check could not be made here, so it has to name what was
unavailable. The id is the stable part and it is what the validator matches on; the
human sentence that follows it in the skip reason is diagnostic text that may be
reworded without touching this file or the gates that read it. The previous version of
this policy matched whole English sentences, so rewording a message silently turned a
declared skip into an undeclared one.
'engines' is the set of engines that are PERMITTED to take the skip. It is not a
prediction and it is not a quota. The same suite takes 14 skips on macOS and may take
fewer on Linux, because a capability is a property of the engine build and the platform
it runs on. The validator therefore never requires a skip to happen; it only ever
rejects one that is not permitted, not evidenced, or contradicted.
'evidence' says how a skip is justified:
probe  -- a control fixture carrying nothing of the site measured the behaviour in
this engine, in this run. The skipping test must carry the measurement as
an annotation, and the independent probe test in measure.spec.ts must have
run on the same engine and agreed. Disagreement is a failure, not a skip.
engine -- a documented, unconditional property of the engine's API surface with no
site-side behaviour to measure. Permitted for a narrow, named API only.

capabilities.note: page.pdf() is implemented over the Chrome DevTools Protocol and Playwright exposes it on Chromium only. There is no site behaviour to measure: the method does not exist to be called. The print stylesheet it exercises is checked on every engine through the print emulation tests, which do not skip.

capabilities.capability: links participate in sequential keyboard navigation
capabilities.probe_test: the tab-ring control fixture is measured, not assumed
capabilities.note: macOS WebKit keeps links out of the tab ring unless the system preference 'Press Tab to highlight each item' is on, and Playwright's WebKit inherits that default. The probe loads a page holding one link and one button and reports what Tab actually reached. A Linux WebKit build that does reach the link arms these checks again with no edit here.

capabilities.capability: a focused overflow container scrolls with the arrow keys
capabilities.probe_test: the keyboard-scroll control fixture is measured, not assumed
capabilities.note: The probe is a 300px box with a 2000px child, a tabindex, no stylesheet and no script. Where ArrowRight does not move it but scrollBy(60) does, the engine cannot express the behaviour at all and a figure frame that does not respond is failing the environment. Where it moves, the check runs against the site.
